source.title: Bounded geometry for PCF-special subvarieties
source.authors: Laura DeMarco, Niki Myrto Mavraki and Hexi Ye
readSections: The entire published open-access article (§§1–5, references), 22 pages, read 2026-09-22 (PDF from Cambridge Core, SHA-256 7845e297f7c154ab6233cb9ea42702e1884764af6b0b6e2b286b62695abe4048); arXiv v3 (10 January 2026) is the accepted version.

summary: Proves that for every degree d and D, the Zariski closure of X ∩ PCF_d, for complex X ⊂ M_d of degree ≤ D, has a uniformly bounded number of components of bounded degree (Theorem 1.1). It also proves that there are finitely many positive-dimensional PCF-special subvarieties of degree ≤ D (Theorem 1.2), with small-critical-height strengthenings over Q̄ (Theorems 1.5, 1.6). All of this is done without classifying PCF-special subvarieties. The key is a relative Bogomolov statement for fibre powers of maximally varying families (Theorem 1.8). Two non-degenerate Yuan–Zhang adelic line bundles built from bifurcation currents give a height inequality and equidistribution. A zooming argument at a parameter where one critical tuple is prerepelling and another critical point is in a parabolic basin shows the two limiting measures differ. The atlas plans canonical heights and equidistribution. It lacks complex bifurcation theory, the critical height and Ingram's theorem, Chow-variety parameter spaces and Yuan–Zhang quasi-projective adelic geometry. The independent review (REV-PAPER-DEMARCO-MAVRAKI-YE-26) confirmed E1–E5 and added four issues. The most significant are two gaps: the witness of Proposition 3.1 is built on the diagonal, where it cannot be transverse when dim ρ₁(X) < r + ℓ (E7), and the §5 induction for Theorem 1.5 in dimension ≥ 2 compares heights of different varieties (E9).

items.name: The moduli space M_d of rational maps
items.statement: For d ≥ 2, M_d is the space of Möbius-conjugacy classes of degree-d maps f : ℙ¹ → ℙ¹: an affine variety of dimension 2d − 2, a geometric quotient over Spec ℤ with a projective GIT compactification defined over ℚ (Silverman), M₂ ≅ ℂ² (Milnor), singular for d > 2.
items.locator: §1, p.1; §2.1, p.5, citing Milnor [Mi1] and Silverman [Si1], Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4
items.note: DY.0 plans iteration, conjugacy and dynamical moduli; the GIT construction of M_d is routed to DY.0 as a source.

items.name: The critically marked cover M_d^cm
items.statement: A finite branched cover M_d^cm → M_d carrying a family f : M_d^cm × ℙ¹ → M_d^cm × ℙ¹ (2.1) of degree-d maps and functions c_i : M_d^cm → ℙ¹, i = 1,…,2d − 2, marking the critical points.
items.note: Routed to DY.0 as a source.

items.name: PCF maps and PCF-special subvarieties
items.statement: f is postcritically finite (PCF) if every critical point has finite forward orbit; PCF_d ⊂ M_d is the set of PCF classes; an irreducible complex subvariety X ⊂ M_d is PCF-special if PCF_d ∩ X is Zariski dense in X (e.g. M_d, the polynomial locus, loci of critical orbit relations).
items.note: Routed to the new Part II ArithmeticDynamicsPartIIBifurcation.

items.name: Flexible Lattès maps and the locus L_d
items.statement: Lattès maps are quotients of self-maps of complex tori; the flexible ones lie in positive-dimensional families, forming the locus L_d ⊂ M_d, which exists only in square degrees; every Lattès map is PCF.
items.locator: §1, p.2; §2.2, p.6, citing Milnor [Mi2], Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4
items.note: Routed to the new Part II.

items.name: Thurston rigidity
items.statement: Every PCF map that is not flexible Lattès is Möbius-conjugate to a map defined over Q̄ (Douady–Hubbard's proof of Thurston's characterization).
items.locator: §2.2, p.6, citing Douady–Hubbard [DH2], Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4
items.note: Routed to the new Part II.

items.name: Call–Silverman canonical height of a rational map
items.statement: For f : ℙ¹ → ℙ¹ of degree d > 1 over Q̄, ĥ_f(x) = lim d^{-n} h(fⁿ(x)).
items.locator: §2.4, p.6, citing Call–Silverman [CS], Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4
items.note: ArithmeticDynamics DY.1 plans canonical heights of polarized morphisms f*L ≅ L^d, with preperiodic points exactly the zeros.

items.name: Weil height on ℙ¹(Q̄)
items.statement: The logarithmic Weil height h used to define ĥ_f.
items.locator: §2.4, p.6, Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4
items.note: Mathlib `Projectivization.logHeight` (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Height/Projectivization.lean:51); the Q̄ extension is RP.0 work.

items.name: The critical height
items.statement: ĥ_crit(f) = Σ_{c : f′(c) = 0} ĥ_f(c) ≥ 0 (critical points with multiplicity), a function on M_d^cm and on M_d(Q̄); for [f] ∈ M_d(Q̄), ĥ_crit(f) = 0 iff f is PCF.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticDynamics DY.6 (canonical heights in families) as a source.

items.name: Ingram: the critical height is a moduli height
items.statement: ĥ_crit is comparable to a Weil height on M_d ∖ L_d: there are constants with c₁ h_{M_d} − c₂ ≤ ĥ_crit ≤ c₃ h_{M_d} + c₄ off the flexible Lattès locus (Silverman's conjecture).
items.locator: §1, p.2; §2.4, p.7, citing Ingram [In]; explicit form [GOV, Thm. C], Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4
items.note: Routed to DY.6 as a source.

items.name: The critical height as an adelic height, and equidistribution of PCF maps
items.statement: ĥ_crit is the height of a non-degenerate adelically metrized line bundle on M_d^cm over Q̄: the restriction to the ramification divisor of the f-invariant adelic line bundle L_f on M_d^cm × ℙ¹, with archimedean curvature T_bif. Galois orbits of generic sequences of PCF parameters equidistribute to the bifurcation measure T_bif^{∧(2d−2)} (Gauthier; Yuan–Zhang).
items.locator: §2.4, p.7, citing Yuan–Zhang [YZ, §6.3], Gauthier [Ga3], Favre–Gauthier [FG1], Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4
items.note: A dynamical application of equidistribution. Routed to ArithmeticDynamics DY.4 as a source.

items.name: Chow varieties of bounded-degree cycles
items.statement: For an irreducible quasi-projective Y ⊂ ℙ^N over Q̄ with closure Ȳ, Ch(Ȳ, r, D) is the Chow variety of r-dimensional cycles of degree ≤ D supported in Ȳ, a subvariety of Ch(ℙ^N, r, D) defined over Q̄. Ch(Y, r, D) is its open subset of cycles meeting Y, and "degree ≤ D" for subvarieties of Y is independent of the embedding up to changing D.
items.locator: §2.5, p.7, citing Gelfand–Kapranov–Zelevinsky [GKZ] and Kollár [Ko], Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4
items.note: Routed to AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.1–R09.2 (parameter spaces and boundedness) as a source.

items.name: Heights on Chow varieties
items.statement: A height h_Ch on each Ch(M_d, r, D), for instance a Philippon height of cycles; h_Ch(X) for a subvariety X of degree ≤ D.
items.locator: §1, p.2; §2.5, p.7, citing Philippon [Ph], Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4
items.note: Heights of subvarieties are already in the uniformity Part II (DGH21 route); routed there.

items.name: Gao–Ge–Kühne Lemma 4.3 (products in a proper subvariety)
items.statement: Let Σ be a subset of a projective variety X with an ample L. If Σ^M lies in a proper subvariety Y ⊂ X^M for some M ≥ 1, then Σ lies in a proper subvariety Z ⊂ X. The number of components of Z and their degrees are bounded in terms of M, dim X, deg X and the total degree of Y (degrees on X^M with respect to ⊠ p_i*L).
items.locator: §5, pp.18–19, citing Gao–Ge–Kühne [GGK, Lemma 4.3], Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4
items.note: Already routed by PAPER-GAO-GE-KUHNE-26 to HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructionsPartII; routed there again, as a consumer, not duplicated.

items.name: Theorem 1.1 (uniform geometry of PCF points)
items.statement: For d ≥ 2 and D ≥ 1 there are B = B(D,d) and N = N(D,d) such that for every complex algebraic subvariety X ⊂ M_d of degree ≤ D, the Zariski closure of X ∩ PCF_d has at most N irreducible components, each of degree ≤ B. Degrees are measured with respect to a fixed very ample line bundle on M_d (for example from Silverman's compactification), and B, N depend on that choice.
items.locator: Theorem 1.1, p.1; proof §5, pp.18–20, Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4 (flexible Lattès points not defined over Q̄ are omitted in the proof, sourceIssues E4)
items.note: A "uniform Dynamical André–Oort" obtained without classifying PCF-special subvarieties (Remark 1.7).

items.name: Theorem 1.2 (finiteness of bounded-degree PCF-special subvarieties)
items.statement: For d ≥ 2 and D ≥ 1 there are only finitely many positive-dimensional irreducible PCF-special subvarieties of M_d of degree ≤ D.
items.locator: Theorem 1.2, p.2; proof §5, Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4
items.note: Consequences: the irreducible components of Per_n(0) have degrees growing with n (Example 1.3).

items.name: Examples 1.3–1.4 (degree growth of Per_n(0), and uniform bound on Per₁(λ))
items.statement: The degrees of the irreducible components of Per_n(0) ⊂ M_d grow with n. There is N with #(Per₁(λ) ∩ PCF₂) ≤ N for all λ ≠ 0 (Per₁(λ) ⊂ M₂ the quadratic maps with a fixed point of multiplier λ, PCF-special iff λ = 0 [DWY]); similarly for Per_n(λ) in the cubic polynomial moduli space.
items.locator: Examples 1.3–1.4, p.2 (misprint E6: PCF_d for PCF₂), citing DeMarco–Wang–Ye [DWY], Baker–DeMarco [BD, Thm. 1.1], Favre–Gauthier [FG2, Thm. B], Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4
items.note: Corollaries of Theorems 1.1–1.2 with the cited special-curve results. Routed to the new Part II.

items.name: Theorem 1.5 (critical-height gap principle)
items.statement: For d ≥ 2 and D ≥ 1 there are B, N and ε = ε(D,d) > 0 such that for every irreducible X ⊂ M_d over Q̄ of degree ≤ D and every 0 ≤ ε′ < ε, the Zariski closure of X ∩ {z ∈ M_d(Q̄) : ĥ_crit(z) ≤ ε′ max{1, h_Ch(X)}} has at most N components, each of degree ≤ B.
items.locator: Theorem 1.5, p.2; proof §5, pp.18–20, Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4 (misprint E3; for r ≥ 2 the induction step of §5 is incomplete, sourceIssues E9)
items.note: Routed to the new Part II. The proof for subvarieties of dimension ≥ 2 needs the repair described in E9; the curve case and Theorems 1.1, 1.2 and 1.6 do not depend on it.

items.name: Essential minimum of the critical height
items.statement: ess.min.(ĥ_crit|_Y) = sup_{Y′ ⊊ Y} inf_{y ∈ (Y ∖ Y′)(Q̄)} ĥ_crit(y) for Y ⊂ M_d over Q̄; PCF-special subvarieties are defined over Q̄ and have essential minimum 0.
items.locator: §1, pp.2–3, Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4
items.note: Routed to the new Part II.

items.name: Theorem 1.6 (small essential minimum)
items.statement: For d ≥ 2 and D ≥ 1 there is ε″ = ε″(d,D) > 0 such that only finitely many positive-dimensional irreducible Y ⊂ M_d over Q̄ of degree ≤ D satisfy ess.min.(ĥ_crit|_Y) ≤ ε″ max{1, h_Ch(Y)}.
items.locator: Theorem 1.6, p.3; proof §5, Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4
items.note: Strengthens Theorem 1.2. Routed to the new Part II.

items.name: Maximally varying families and fibre powers
items.statement: A family X → V of r-dimensional X_λ ⊂ Y over an irreducible quasi-projective V of dimension ℓ ≥ 1, with geometrically irreducible generic fibre, is maximally varying if V → Ch(Y, r, D), λ ↦ [X_λ], has finite fibres; X^m_V is the m-th fibre power with ρ_m : X^m_V → Y^m, (λ, f₁,…,f_m) ↦ (f₁,…,f_m).
items.note: Routed to the new Part II.

items.name: Proposition 2.1 (maximal variation makes ρ_ℓ generically finite)
items.statement: If X → V is maximally varying with V and the generic fibre irreducible and dim V = ℓ ≥ 1, then ρ_ℓ : X^ℓ_V → Y^ℓ is generically finite; in particular dim ρ_ℓ(X^ℓ_V) = ℓ(r + 1).
items.locator: Proposition 2.1 and proof, pp.7–8, Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4
items.note: Induction on ℓ by slicing with a codimension-(r+1) subvariety through a regular point. Routed to the new Part II.

items.name: Theorem 1.8 (relative critical-height Bogomolov)
items.statement: Let X → V be a maximally varying family of r-dimensional (r ≥ 1) subvarieties of M_d over an irreducible quasi-projective V of dimension ℓ ≥ 1, all over Q̄, with geometrically irreducible generic fibre. There is ε = ε(X) > 0 such that Z_ε(X) = {(λ, f₁,…,f_{ℓ+1}) ∈ X^{ℓ+1}_V(Q̄) : Σ_i ĥ_crit(f_i) < ε max{1, h_Ch(λ)}} is not Zariski dense in X^{ℓ+1}_V.
items.locator: Theorem 1.8, p.4; proof §4, pp.13–18, Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4 (misprint E5 in (4.3); E8 in (4.4); the witness from Proposition 3.1 needs E7)
items.note: Two non-degenerate adelic line bundles M₁, M₂ on X^{ℓ+1}_V, built from two r-tuples of critical points, give a height inequality (4.6) by [YZ, Thm. 1.3.2]. The measure c₁(L̄)^{∧(r+1)ℓ} on X^ℓ_V is only ≥ α₁µ_ℓ, not equal to it (E8); the argument runs with it in place of µ_ℓ. If small points were dense, Yuan–Zhang equidistribution would force the measures µ^{r+1}_λ and µ¹_λ to be proportional on X_λ (4.8). Zooming at a parameter where one tuple is transversely prerepelling while c_{r+1} is in a parabolic basin contradicts this (Lemma 4.1, [Ga2, Prop. 3.2]). Routed to the new Part II.

items.name: Positive closed currents with continuous potentials and their wedge products
items.statement: Positive closed (1,1)-currents with continuous local potentials on complex manifolds and varieties, their pullbacks and pushforwards, and Bedford–Taylor wedge products, continuous under locally uniform convergence of potentials.
items.locator: §§2.3, 3, 4 (throughout), Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4
items.note: Pluripotential foundations; no atlas layer owns currents. Routed to the new Part II.

items.name: Bifurcation currents and the bifurcation measure
items.statement: With ω̂ the pullback of a Fubini–Study form, T̂_f = lim d^{-n}(fⁿ)*ω̂ on M_d^cm × ℙ¹. T_i = π_*(T̂_f ∧ [Γ_{c_i}]) (2.2) is a positive (1,1)-current with continuous potentials, and T_i ∧ T_i = 0. T_bif = Σ_i T_i (2.3) descends to M_d and equals DeMarco's bifurcation current, and the bifurcation measure T_bif^{∧(2d−2)} is non-zero (Bassanelli–Berteloot). For product maps Φ = (f₁,…,f_m) the Green current is T̂_Φ = Σ p_i*T̂_{f_i}.
items.locator: §2.3, (2.2)–(2.3), p.6; (3.2), pp.10–11, citing Dujardin–Favre [DF], DeMarco [De1], Bassanelli–Berteloot [BB], Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4
items.note: Routed to the new Part II.

items.name: Activity and non-vanishing of bifurcation currents
items.statement: For an irreducible X ⊂ M_d^cm of dimension r > 0 whose image is not in L_d: T_bif ≠ 0 on X [McMullen, Lemma 2.2; DeMarco, Thm. 1.1]; T_i = 0 on X iff c_i is persistently preperiodic along X [DF, Thm. 2.5]; and T_bif^{∧r} ≠ 0 on X, so some r-tuple has T_{i₁} ∧ ⋯ ∧ T_{i_r} ≠ 0 [GOV, Lemma 6.8].
items.locator: §2.3, p.6; §3, p.9, citing McMullen [Mc1], DeMarco [De1], Dujardin–Favre [DF], Gauthier–Okuyama–Vigny [GOV], Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4
items.note: Routed to the new Part II.

items.name: Prerepelling parameters and supports of bifurcation currents
items.statement: An m-tuple a of marked points is transversely (resp. properly) prerepelling for Φ = (f₁,…,f_m) at λ₀ if each a_i lands on a repelling periodic point and the graphs of the landing maps and the continued repelling points meet transversely (resp. properly). Dujardin: for a single family (f₁ = ⋯ = f_m = f) and m ≤ 2d − 2 marked critical points, parameters where (c₁,…,c_m) is transversely prerepelling are dense in supp T₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ T_m [Du, Thm. 1.1]. Conversely, a properly prerepelling tuple over a parameter space of dimension ≥ m lies in the support of the corresponding wedge product; for rigid repellers of product maps, T̂_Φ^{∧m} ∧ [Γ_c] ≠ 0 [BE; Ga1, Thm. 6.2; Ga2, Thm. 2.3; BBD, Prop. 3.7; DM1, Prop. 4.8].
items.locator: §3, p.9, Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4
items.note: Routed to the new Part II.

items.name: Proposition 3.1 (the measure µ_ℓ on X^ℓ_V)
items.statement: For a maximally varying family X → V of r-dimensional varieties in M_d^cm with dim V = ℓ ≥ 1, π₁*(T_bif^{∧(r+1)}) ∧ ⋯ ∧ π_ℓ*(T_bif^{∧(r+1)}) ∧ [ρ_ℓ(X^ℓ_V)] ≠ 0, so µ_ℓ = ρ_ℓ*(…) is a non-zero positive measure on X^ℓ_V, witnessed by an ℓ(r+1)-tuple of marked critical points transversely prerepelling for (f₁,…,f₁,…,f_ℓ,…,f_ℓ) at some parameter.
items.locator: Proposition 3.1 and proof, pp.9–11, Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4 (misprint E1; gap E7 in the construction of the witness)
items.note: Routed to the new Part II. The proof builds the witness at a diagonal point (y₀, …, y₀), where ρ_ℓ has positive-dimensional fibres whenever dim ρ₁(X) < r + ℓ; the non-vanishing of µ_ℓ stands, but the witness must be found off the diagonal (E7).

items.name: J-stability and parabolic parameters
items.statement: In a holomorphic family where a marked critical point is active, parameters with a parabolic cycle are dense in its bifurcation locus (Mañé–Sad–Sullivan), and by polynomial-like renormalization (Douady–Hubbard) the critical point lies in the parabolic basin at such parameters; the bifurcation locus of an active marked critical point in a one-parameter family has no isolated points.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 3.2, pp.12–13, citing Mañé–Sad–Sullivan [MSS], Douady–Hubbard [DH1], Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4
items.note: Routed to the new Part II.

items.name: Proposition 3.2 (two measures on X^{ℓ+1}_V)
items.statement: If c witnesses µ_ℓ ≠ 0, there are x₀ = (λ₀, t₁,…,t_ℓ), x₁ = (λ₁, s₁,…,s_ℓ) ∈ supp µ_ℓ and indices i ≠ j such that: (1) the r-tuple omitting c_{ℓ,i} is transversely prerepelling for F(λ₀) at t_ℓ over X_{λ₀}; (2) the r-tuple omitting c_{ℓ,j} is properly prerepelling there; (3) the r-tuple omitting c_{ℓ,i} is transversely prerepelling for F(λ₁) at s_ℓ over X_{λ₁}; (4) c_{ℓ,i} is attracted to a parabolic cycle at s_ℓ. Hence µ^i_ℓ = Π₁*(µ_ℓ) ∧ Π₂*(⋀_{k≠i} T_{c_{ℓ,k}}) and µ^j_ℓ are non-zero on X^{ℓ+1}_V.
items.locator: Proposition 3.2 and proof, pp.11–13, Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4
items.note: Routed to the new Part II.

items.name: Slicing of measures along a projection
items.statement: For a product-type measure on X^{ℓ+1}_V = X^ℓ_V ×_V X, integration against test functions disintegrates along the projection to X^ℓ_V ([BB, Prop. 4.3]), giving (4.7) and, by weak continuity of the fibre measures, the fibrewise proportionality (4.8) for λ ∈ supp π_*µ_ℓ.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 1.8, (4.7)–(4.8), pp.15–16, citing [BB, Prop. 4.3] and [MaS, Thm. 1.8], Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4
items.note: Routed to the new Part II.

items.name: Lemma 4.1 (orbits in a parabolic basin under exponential zoom)
items.statement: Let f : 𝔻^r × ℙ¹ → 𝔻^r × ℙ¹ be a holomorphic family of degree-d maps with a marked critical point c such that c(0) is attracted to a parabolic fixed point z = 0 of f₀. For every ρ > 1 there is δ > 0 such that α_n(x) = f^n_{x/ρⁿ}(c(x/ρⁿ)) → 0 uniformly on 𝔻_δ^r.
items.locator: Lemma 4.1 and proof, pp.16–17, Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4 (misprint E2)
items.note: Routed to the new Part II.

items.name: Rescaling limit at a transversely prerepelling parameter (Buff–Epstein, Gauthier)
items.statement: If an r-tuple of critical points is transversely prerepelling at s ∈ X_λ, the zooms r_n : 𝔻^r → X_λ at the exponential rates given by the repelling multipliers satisfy d^{nr} r_n*(T_{c₁} ∧ ⋯ ∧ T_{c_r}) → µ ≠ 0 ([BE, §3]; [Ga2, Prop. 3.2]).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 1.8, (4.11), p.18, Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4
items.note: Routed to the new Part II.

items.name: Yuan–Zhang adelic line bundles on quasi-projective varieties
items.statement: The group P̂ic(X)_{ℚ,nef} of nef adelic line bundles on a quasi-projective X over a number field. The invariant extension L_Φ of a polarization for a polarized dynamical family Φ [YZ, Thm. 6.1.1]. The Deligne pairing ⟨L|_{Γ_c}⟩ of relative dimension 0 along the graph of a section [YZ, Thm. 4.2.3, §4.2, §6.2.2]. Heights, curvature measures and non-degeneracy, where M is non-degenerate iff c₁(M)^{∧dim} ≠ 0 [YZ, Lemma 5.4].
items.locator: §4, pp.13–14, citing Yuan–Zhang [YZ], Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4
items.note: Routed to ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeightsPartII, the pending Part II of Yuan–Zhang adelic geometry.

items.name: Yuan–Zhang height inequality
items.statement: For a non-degenerate nef adelic line bundle M on a quasi-projective X over Q̄ and a height h on a base, there are ε₁, ε₂ > 0 and a Zariski open dense U ⊂ X with h_M ≥ ε₁ h − ε₂ on U(Q̄) ([YZ, Thm. 1.3.2]).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 1.8, (4.6), p.15, citing [YZ, Thm. 1.3.2], Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4
items.note: Routed to ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeightsPartII.

items.name: Yuan–Zhang fundamental inequality and equidistribution
items.statement: For nef non-degenerate M on quasi-projective X over Q̄, a generic sequence of small points forces h_M(X) = 0 ([YZ, Thm. 5.3.3]), and then Galois orbits of a generic small sequence equidistribute to c₁(M)^{∧dim X}/vol ([YZ, Thm. 5.4.3]).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 1.8, p.15, citing [YZ, Thms. 5.3.3, 5.4.3], Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e4
items.note: Routed to ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeightsPartII.

routes.reason: DY.0 owns dynamical moduli, DY.4 equidistribution of small points with dynamical applications, and DY.6 canonical heights in families. The paper is a source for the moduli space M_d of rational maps and its critically marked cover, for the critical height and Ingram's comparison with a moduli height, and for arithmetic equidistribution of PCF parameters to the bifurcation measure (Gauthier; Yuan–Zhang §6.3). These are arithmetic-dynamics foundations that the planned layers name but do not yet construct.

R09.1–R09.2 own projective parameter spaces, boundedness and Hilbert schemes. The paper parametrizes subvarieties of M_d of bounded degree by Chow varieties Ch(M_d, r, D), a parameter space in the same direction (Kollár, GKZ).

routes.title: Arakelov geometry and heights of abelian varieties, Part II: adelic bigness on curve families
routes.brief: This is the Part II proposed by PAPER-YUAN-26 (and used by PAPER-GAO-HABEGGER-19) under the same id, and its brief remains binding. This paper consumes the Yuan–Zhang theory of adelic line bundles on quasi-projective varieties over number fields beyond curve families. Add: nef adelic line bundles P̂ic(X)_{ℚ,nef}; invariant extensions L_Φ of a polarization for a polarized family of endomorphisms (Yuan–Zhang, arXiv:2105.13587, Thm. 6.1.1); the relative-dimension-0 Deligne pairing ⟨L|_{Γ_c}⟩ along the graph of a section (Thm. 4.2.3, §6.2.2); the non-degeneracy criterion c₁(M)^{∧dim X} ≠ 0 (Lemma 5.4); the height inequality h_M ≥ ε₁h − ε₂ on a dense open set for non-degenerate M (Thm. 1.3.2); the fundamental inequality (Thm. 5.3.3); and equidistribution of generic small sequences (Thm. 5.4.3). Export them to ArithmeticDynamicsPartIIBifurcation. Acceptance: for a polarized map of ℙ¹ the invariant extension recovers the Call–Silverman height, and for the critically marked family the restriction to the ramification divisor gives the critical height.
routes.reason: Yuan–Zhang adelic geometry on quasi-projective varieties is the content of the pending Part II proposed by YUAN-26. This paper needs its general height inequality and equidistribution, so it coalesces there.

routes.title: Heights, rational points and obstructions, Part II: uniform Bogomolov and uniform Mordell–Lang
routes.brief: This is the Part II proposed by PAPER-YUAN-26, PAPER-GAO-GE-KUHNE-26, PAPER-DIMITROV-GAO-HABEGGER-21 and PAPER-GAO-HABEGGER-19 under the same id, and their briefs remain binding. This paper adds only consumers, so nothing is duplicated. The first is the height h_Ch of cycles on Chow varieties Ch(Y, r, D), for instance Philippon's height (Math. Ann. 289 (1991)); the DGH21 route already asks for heights of subvarieties. The second is Gao–Ge–Kühne Lemma 4.3, already routed here by GAO-GE-KUHNE-26: if Σ^M lies in a proper subvariety of X^M then Σ lies in a proper subvariety with number and degrees of components bounded by M, dim X, deg X and the degree of the subvariety. State the lemma for a quasi-projective X with its closure and for subvarieties defined over ℂ, as ArithmeticDynamicsPartIIBifurcation uses it. Acceptance: the bound depends only on the listed quantities and not on Σ.
routes.reason: Heights of cycles and the GGK product lemma are already part of the uniformity Part II. This paper only consumes them.

routes.title: Arithmetic dynamics, Part II: bifurcation currents and PCF-special subvarieties

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Theorems 1.1 and 1.2, §5, pp.19–20 (complex parameters) (published version)
sourceIssues.printed: "… and to Σ_{λ,ε} := {f ∈ C_λ ∩ M_d(Q̄) : ĥ_crit(f) < ε/(ℓ+1)} ⊂ C_λ for λ ∈ U(ℂ) ∖ U(Q̄) … repeating this procedure provides uniform bounds on the Zariski closures of Σ^r_{λ,ε′} for all ε′ < ε and of X_λ ∩ PCF_d for all λ ∈ U(ℂ)."
sourceIssues.correction: For λ ∈ V(ℂ) ∖ V(Q̄), X_λ ∩ PCF_d can contain flexible Lattès maps not defined over Q̄. These do not lie in Σ_{λ,ε}, whose points are in M_d(Q̄). Since X_λ ∩ PCF_d ∖ M_d(Q̄) ⊂ L_d (Thurston rigidity, §2.2), add the components of X_λ ∩ L_d. By Bézout they number at most D·deg L_d plus the number of components of L_d, with degrees ≤ max{deg L_d, 1}, uniformly in λ. The theorems are unaffected; only N and B change.
sourceIssues.reason: The count in §5 bounds only algebraic points of small critical height, but Theorem 1.1 is stated for arbitrary complex X and all PCF points. Flexible Lattès maps are PCF and form a curve L_d ⊂ M_d in square degrees whose points with transcendental j-invariant are not defined over Q̄. So for d a square and transcendental λ, a curve C_λ can meet L_d in PCF points outside Σ_{λ,ε}.

sourceIssues.printed: "In this way, we inductively construct a parameter y = (y₀, …, y₀) ∈ Y_ℓ and an ℓ(r + 1)-tuple of marked critical points c … which is transversely prerepelling for the map Φ at y over Y_ℓ. … Finally, since the map from X^ℓ_V to Y_ℓ is generically finite by Proposition 2.1, our initial choice of y₀ guarantees that the marked critical points c are also transversely prerepelling at a preimage of y, over X^ℓ_V."
sourceIssues.correction: The witness must be found at a point of supp µ_ℓ where ρ_ℓ is a local isomorphism, which is off the diagonal whenever dim ρ₁(X) < r + ℓ. One route is a density theorem for transversely prerepelling parameters, in the style of [Du, Theorem 1.1], for the product family Φ over X^ℓ_V applied to the non-zero measure ρ_ℓ^*(⋀ T_{c_{i,j}}). The paper states Dujardin's theorem only for a single family (f, …, f). The conclusion µ_ℓ ≠ 0 is not affected: it uses (3.2) over Y_ℓ, where the intersection at y is isolated.
sourceIssues.reason: The construction uses the same point y₀ in every factor, so y lies on the diagonal. Let k = dim ρ₁(X). The preimage ρ_ℓ^{−1}(y) contains {(λ′, y₀, …, y₀) : y₀ ∈ X_{λ′}}, which has dimension r + ℓ − k, the fibre dimension of ρ₁ that the proof itself fixes over U. The paper allows k < r + ℓ, and in §5, where V is a whole component of Ch(M_d, r, D), that is the usual case. All ℓ(r + 1) landing conditions depend only on (f₁, …, f_ℓ), so they hold along this fibre. Hence c is not even properly prerepelling at any preimage of y, and generic finiteness of ρ_ℓ says nothing on the diagonal. Example: the lines in M₂ ≅ ℂ² (ℓ = 2, r = 1, k = 2). The preimage of (y₀, y₀) is the pencil of lines through y₀. The curve Γ of Proposition 3.2's proof is then {(λ, y₀) : y₀ ∈ X_λ}, along which the map is constant, so c_{ℓ,r+1} is not active along Γ as that proof requires.

sourceIssues.locator: §5, the induction step for r > 1, p.20 (published version)
sourceIssues.printed: "Note that Σ^r_{λ,ε} is not necessarily Zariski dense in Z(λ), so we apply the induction hypotheses (specifically, the constants from each of the statements of Theorems 1.1, 1.2, 1.5, 1.6 for subvarieties of dimension < r) to each irreducible component Y(λ) of Z(λ), for all λ ∈ U(ℂ). Thus, by reducing ε if needed, we conclude that the Zariski-closure of Σ^r_{λ,ε} ∩ Y(λ) has uniformly bounded number of components, each with uniformly bounded degree for all λ ∈ U(ℂ)."
sourceIssues.correction: For λ ∈ U(Q̄) the step needs a uniform bound for the Zariski closure of Y(λ) ∩ {ĥ_crit < (ε/(ℓ+1)) max{1, h_Ch(λ)}}, a threshold measured against the ambient X_λ. Either prove Theorem 1.5 in that relative form (for Y ⊂ X of bounded degrees, with threshold ε max{1, h_Ch(X)}), so that the induction closes, or show h_Ch(Y(λ)) ≥ c h_Ch(λ) − c′ for the components that occur. Theorems 1.1, 1.2 and 1.6, and the curve case of Theorem 1.5, do not use a height-scaled threshold on Y(λ) and are unaffected.
sourceIssues.reason: The induction hypothesis (Theorem 1.5 for Y(λ)) controls only Y(λ) ∩ {ĥ_crit ≤ ε′ max{1, h_Ch(Y(λ))}}, and nothing bounds h_Ch(λ) by a multiple of h_Ch(Y(λ)). Reducing ε by a constant therefore does not bring one set inside the other. For instance, if a fixed Y lies in X_λ for all λ in a positive-dimensional W ⊂ V, then h_Ch(λ) is unbounded on W(Q̄) while h_Ch(Y) is fixed. For suitable λ the threshold then falls between ε′ max{1, h_Ch(Y)} and the essential minimum of ĥ_crit on Y, where the small points of Y are not dense and neither Theorem 1.5 nor Theorem 1.6 for Y bounds how many there are.
